Top candidates: Physoderma_Brown_Spot (banded oval spots), Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight (rectangular tan lesions), Northern_Leaf_Blight (cigar-shaped lesions).

The banded distribution of oval tan spots most suggests Physoderma_Brown_Spot. Viewing one reference:

The Physoderma Brown Spot reference shows very tiny, densely packed small spots (not matching) with dark midrib lesions. The test image has larger, more discrete oval/rectangular tan lesions - clearly different from the Physoderma pattern.

Reconsidering based on test image features:
- Discrete oval to somewhat rectangular tan/brown lesions, ~2-3 cm
- Multiple lesions scattered across the leaf  
- Some with slightly darker borders
- Not tiny/dense (rules out Physoderma Brown Spot)
- Not cigar-shaped elongated (less likely Northern Leaf Blight)
- No pustules (rules out rust)
- No streaks/mosaic (rules out viral)

The lesions match **Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight** - oval at first becoming rectangular, light brown with darker brown margin, confined by leaf veins, up to 2.5 cm long.
